requirements.statement: AAV is an engineered particle: the capsid influences cell entry, the cassette decides what could be made, and address is not payload job.
requirements.note: Definition now source-read: capsid shell protects the genome and mediates binding and entry; variants differ in tropism; the cassette is the designed payload. Review source (OA full text).
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: AAV is an engineered particle: the capsid influences cell entry, the cassette decides what could be made, and address is not payload job.

requirements.statement: Delivered DNA must reach the nucleus and act as a transcription template before RNA and protein; DNA location and expression are separate layers (figure).
requirements.note: Adds the review's statement that single-stranded AAV DNA must become double-stranded before expression, a step between DNA arrival and RNA.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Delivered DNA must reach the nucleus and act as a transcription template before RNA and protein; DNA location and expression are separate layers (figure).

requirements.statement: Episomes are DNA outside chromosomes; sampled human muscle held persistent circular vector genomes whose recovered sequences were expression-competent (tissue- and construct-specific).
requirements.note: Abstract only; PMC full text blocked (challenge page).
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Episomes are DNA outside chromosomes; sampled human muscle held persistent circular vector genomes whose recovered sequences were expression-competent (tissue- and construct-specific).

requirements.statement: Episomal genomes can be lost on cell division; mouse liver regeneration separated extrachromosomal from integrated forms and expression.
requirements.note: Full text retrieved (PMC HTML); abstract used for the claim.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Episomal genomes can be lost on cell division; mouse liver regeneration separated extrachromosomal from integrated forms and expression.

requirements.statement: 'Often episomal' is not 'never integrates'; persistent DNA does not ensure an intact cassette, adequate protein or a surviving functional cell.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: 'Often episomal' is not 'never integrates'; persistent DNA does not ensure an intact cassette, adequate protein or a surviving functional cell.

requirements.statement: Capsid-directed immunity can reduce delivery or persistence: human liver study showed expression loss alongside evidence of immunity against transduced cells.
requirements.note: Abstract only; Nature Medicine full text not retrieved.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Capsid-directed immunity can reduce delivery or persistence: human liver study showed expression loss alongside evidence of immunity against transduced cells.

requirements.statement: Re-dosing: neutralising antibodies against the capsid make re-administration difficult; whether a product can be given again is product-specific.
requirements.note: Resolved: Naso review (OA full text) and Rana 2024 (abstract and OA full text; C57BL/6 and hemophilia mouse work). The mouse B-cell depletion protocol is stated as not a clinical option.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Re-dosing: neutralising antibodies against the capsid make re-administration difficult; whether a product can be given again is product-specific.

requirements.statement: AAV inside T-cell genome-editing workflows: AAV6 can carry a donor repair template into electroporated T cells while Cas9 mRNA and guide RNA make the cut; the lasting change is the knocked-in receptor, not direct AAV targeting of T cells in a patient.
requirements.note: Resolved with Eyquem 2017 (abstract and PMC author-manuscript HTML read). Setting: primary human T cells in culture plus a mouse leukaemia model.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: AAV inside T-cell genome-editing workflows: AAV6 can carry a donor repair template into electroporated T cells while Cas9 mRNA and guide RNA make the cut; the lasting change is the knocked-in receptor, not direct AAV targeting of T cells in a patient.

requirements.statement: Packaging capacity: oversized plasmid-encoded vectors (4.7 to 8.7 kb) in AAV2/5/8 packaged at no more than 5.2 kb, truncated at the 5' end and less efficiently expressed than genomes under 5 kb; a multi-component design cannot assume all sequences fit.
requirements.note: Wu full text remains access-failed (PMC, SAGE-style challenge); the claim is limited to the abstract, which states the in vitro, high-MOI expression qualification and the authors' recombination proposal. Row now fully covers what the abstract supports; full-text confirmation remains a retained access limit.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Packaging capacity: oversized plasmid-encoded vectors (4.7 to 8.7 kb) in AAV2/5/8 packaged at no more than 5.2 kb, truncated at the 5' end and less efficiently expressed than genomes under 5 kb; a multi-component design cannot assume all sequences fit.

requirements.statement: Scope of the 4.7 kb statement: AAV2 single-stranded genome is 4,675 nucleotides; reviews give about 4.8 kb for AAV genomes and about 3.3 kb of capacity for self-complementary designs; not a universal packaging limit.
requirements.note: Resolved by scope. Srivastava 1983 (Europe PMC abstract; PMC page header) fixes AAV2 at 4,675 nt; Naso review gives about 4.8 kb and the self-complementary reduction; Wu shows packaged genomes up to 5.2 kb in three capsids. The Guide's 'about 4.7 kb wild-type' is consistent with AAV2 but is not a universal limit and is stated in the record as genome sizes of named viruses and designs.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Distinguish the named AAV2 genome sequence, measured packaged-genome lengths and usable coding capacity. Self-complementary designs trade coding capacity for an inverted repeat that can pair with itself; do not infer one universal packaging ceiling.

requirements.statement: AAV usual genetic behaviour gives no universal safety advantage; assessment is product-specific (FDA long-term follow-up guidance).
requirements.note: FDA says non-integrating vectors generally carry a lower delayed-risk; the applied record states that nuance rather than the Guide's flatter wording.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: AAV usual genetic behaviour gives no universal safety advantage; assessment is product-specific (FDA long-term follow-up guidance).

requirements.statement: Measurement: vector genome copies per stated denominator; sequence and DNA-form analyses for integrity, episomes or integration; RNA and protein in identified cells; copy counts cannot determine location or antitumour function.
requirements.note: Measurement points covered with evidence: biopsies sample limited regions at stated times; per-cell genome numbers and form analyses differ from copy counts; copy counts do not show an intact cassette. No source gives acceptance thresholds, and the Guide states none (criteria are construct- and assay-specific).
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Measurement: vector genome copies per stated denominator; sequence and DNA-form analyses for integrity, episomes or integration; RNA and protein in identified cells; copy counts cannot determine location or antitumour function.

requirements.statement: Common confusions: nonintegrating category is not zero integration; persistence is not survival through every division; capsid targeting is not cancer targeting.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Common confusions: nonintegrating category is not zero integration; persistence is not survival through every division; capsid targeting is not cancer targeting.

requirements.statement: Inference from the muscle-to-CAR persistence example: a long-lived expression result in human muscle cannot be assigned to rapidly dividing T cells carrying a different cassette; test genome form and expression in the intended cells.
requirements.note: Extracted from the fictional Try it and Explain-it-back. Evidence: episomes persist in slowly turning-over muscle and are diluted on division (Naso, Nakai); a T-cell workflow uses a different design (Eyquem).
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Inference from the muscle-to-CAR persistence example: a long-lived expression result in human muscle cannot be assigned to rapidly dividing T cells carrying a different cassette; test genome form and expression in the intended cells.

requirements.statement: Takeaway restates R02, R03, R05, R12: assess entry, DNA fate, expression and function in intended cells.
requirements.note: Points to the exact evidence of the rows it restates.

requirements.statement: Lentiviral vectors package an RNA genome; after entry reverse transcription makes DNA; in an integrating design integrase inserts it; an internal promoter drives the cassette; this is transduction; envelope influences entry (pseudotyping) not what a CAR recognises.
requirements.note: Adds Milone review (OA full text): env encodes the envelope glycoprotein and entry depends on glycoprotein binding. The term 'pseudotyping' itself is not defined in any retrieved text (Milone cites Burns 1993, unread); the record states only that the envelope influences entry and that this is distinct from what an encoded receptor recognises (reasoning).
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Lentiviral vectors package an RNA genome; after entry reverse transcription makes DNA; in an integrating design integrase inserts it; an internal promoter drives the cassette; this is transduction; envelope influences entry (pseudotyping) not what a CAR recognises.

requirements.statement: Replication-defective does not replace testing for replication-competent virus.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Replication-defective does not replace testing for replication-competent virus.

requirements.statement: Self-inactivating: LTR regulatory sequences disabled, internal promoter can still express; SIN does not mean the cassette removes itself or cannot integrate.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Self-inactivating: LTR regulatory sequences disabled, internal promoter can still express; SIN does not mean the cassette removes itself or cannot integrate.

requirements.statement: An integrated cassette can be inherited on division but does not guarantee survival, stable expression, tumour entry or killing; integration sites, copy number and clonality bear on insertional-mutagenesis assessment; risk is product-specific, not a viral-versus-nonviral ranking.

requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Inference from the Try it: 'nonviral, ex vivo transposon-engineered CAR T cells' does not mean 'nonintegrating' or 'injected to engineer cells in the body'; genetic fate and engineering location are separate.

requirements.statement: Source scope: Ivics 1997 (mechanism in defined cells), Kebriaei 2016 (early ex vivo phase I workflow), Huang 2010 (insertion preferences in specified primary T-cell experiments) and FDA long-term follow-up guidance; no ranking of platforms.
requirements.note: Identities verified.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: source-list/scope metadata; source reading retained, not additional teaching credit

requirements.statement: Takeaway restates R02, R05, R08.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: derived takeaway; assessed but not an independent semantic requirement

requirements.statement: Delivery targeting decides which cells receive the intervention; cancer targeting is what the resulting molecule or cell recognises; carrier marker A and receptor antigen B need not match (diagram).
requirements.note: Draft already states the A/B principle; patch adds the three-question structure.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Delivery targeting decides which cells receive the intervention; cancer targeting is what the resulting molecule or cell recognises; carrier marker A and receptor antigen B need not match (diagram).

requirements.statement: Binding or particle uptake may occur without expression; a CAR that binds B may fail to activate or kill; binding, expression, signalling and target-cell effects need separate tests.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Binding or particle uptake may occur without expression; a CAR that binds B may fail to activate or kill; binding, expression, signalling and target-cell effects need separate tests.

requirements.statement: The delivery address can be an antigen-presenting cell in a vaccine; vaccine-carrier targeting is not direct tumour delivery.
requirements.note: Kranz abstract only.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: The delivery address can be an antigen-presenting cell in a vaccine; vaccine-carrier targeting is not direct tumour delivery.

requirements.statement: Comparison tables: three targeting questions (who receives usable cargo; what the receptor recognises; where engineered cells act) with measurement and remaining boundary.
requirements.note: The two comparison tables are mapped to the three questions in the patch prose with evidence for each row (recipient expression, receptor recognition/healthy tissue, where cells act). Table layout itself is not reproduced.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Comparison tables: three targeting questions (who receives usable cargo; what the receptor recognises; where engineered cells act) with measurement and remaining boundary.

requirements.statement: Selective engineering does not remove on-target, off-tumour risk; little unintended-cell expression in a sample does not establish absence.
requirements.note: On-target off-tumour has no OnCo term (queued); patch carries the FDA statement.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Selective engineering does not remove on-target, off-tumour risk; little unintended-cell expression in a sample does not establish absence.

requirements.statement: Measurement card: flow cytometry for receptor-positive fractions in identified subsets; functional assays with matched antigen-positive and antigen-negative controls; percentage among expressing cells differs from percentage of all T cells.
requirements.note: Denominator point sourced by Rurik's share-of-expressing-cells figure.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Measurement card: flow cytometry for receptor-positive fractions in identified subsets; functional assays with matched antigen-positive and antigen-negative controls; percentage among expressing cells differs from percentage of all T cells.

requirements.statement: Inferences from the worked example: report receptor-positive percentages within each sampled population (30% of T cells, 5% of non-T cells) rather than calling delivery exclusive; activity against B-positive healthy cells with little activity against B-negative controls shows B-dependent activity and a safety concern, not selective cancer killing.
requirements.note: Extracted from fictional numbers (60/200=30%, 5/100=5%, verified).
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Inferences from the worked example: report receptor-positive percentages within each sampled population (30% of T cells, 5% of non-T cells) rather than calling delivery exclusive; activity against B-positive healthy cells with little activity against B-negative controls shows B-dependent activity and a safety concern, not selective cancer killing.

requirements.statement: Source scope: Rurik, Hunter, Kranz and FDA CAR T guidance (January 2024).

coordinatorDisposition.kind: source-list/scope metadata; source reading retained, not additional teaching credit

requirements.statement: Takeaway restates R01, R04, R06.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: derived takeaway; assessed but not an independent semantic requirement

requirements.statement: Codon optimisation changes synonymous codons to influence RNA behaviour and protein production while preserving the amino-acid sequence; a codon is three bases; GCU and GCC both specify alanine (figure).
requirements.note: Draft already defines synonymous change.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Codon optimisation changes synonymous codons to influence RNA behaviour and protein production while preserving the amino-acid sequence; a codon is three bases; GCU and GCC both specify alanine (figure).

requirements.statement: tRNA abundance depends on cell and state; codon frequency alone is an incomplete guide; Wu measured codon-dependent RNA decay in human cell lines.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: tRNA abundance depends on cell and state; codon frequency alone is an incomplete guide; Wu measured codon-dependent RNA decay in human cell lines.

requirements.statement: RNA folds by internal pairing; location of structure matters; Mauger separated codon usage from coding-region structure; more structured coding regions could prolong the period of active translation; removing all structure or maximising a codon score is not a universal optimum.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: RNA folds by internal pairing; location of structure matters; Mauger separated codon usage from coding-region structure; more structured coding regions could prolong the period of active translation; removing all structure or maximising a codon score is not a universal optimum.

requirements.statement: 'Optimised' must name an objective and tested context; prediction remains a proposal until measured; nucleoside chemistry, cap, UTRs and delivery also affect the result.
requirements.note: Upgraded from existing-draft-text: the patch states the objective-and-system point with Mauger's definition of functional half-life.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: 'Optimised' must name an objective and tested context; prediction remains a proposal until measured; nucleoside chemistry, cap, UTRs and delivery also affect the result.

requirements.statement: Synonymous redesign does not fix the tumour mutation or change the antigen; more protein cannot establish processing, display or recognition; amino-acid spacers are a separate design change.
requirements.note: Antigen identity versus expression: stated in the draft; no source claims display. Not extended beyond that.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Synonymous redesign does not fix the tumour mutation or change the antigen; more protein cannot establish processing, display or recognition; amino-acid spacers are a separate design change.

requirements.statement: Measurement table: sequence checks, RNA time course, protein quantity or activity; matched RNA amount, chemistry, cap, UTRs, purity, delivery; reporter signal alone cannot establish RNA half-life, translation fidelity, presentation or benefit; transfer to new cell, formulation or antigen needs testing.
requirements.note: Measurement-table claims mapped: time-course decay measures (Wu), reporter versus functional lifetime (Mauger), matched constructs and systems.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Measurement table: sequence checks, RNA time course, protein quantity or activity; matched RNA amount, chemistry, cap, UTRs, purity, delivery; reporter signal alone cannot establish RNA half-life, translation fidelity, presentation or benefit; transfer to new cell, formulation or antigen needs testing.

requirements.statement: Inference from the Try it (reporter 200 versus 100): twice the reporter signal at one time is not twice the RNA lifetime, a better neoantigen or any display; confirm intended protein, use a time course, choose the next assay for the next claim.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Inference from the Try it (reporter 200 versus 100): twice the reporter signal at one time is not twice the RNA lifetime, a better neoantigen or any display; confirm intended protein, use a time course, choose the next assay for the next claim.

requirements.statement: Source scope: Wu 2019 and Mauger 2019 as primary cell/reporter studies.
requirements.note: Identities verified.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: source-list/scope metadata; source reading retained, not additional teaching credit

requirements.statement: Takeaway restates R04, R06.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: derived takeaway; assessed but not an independent semantic requirement

requirements.statement: IVT makes RNA from a DNA template with an RNA polymerase outside living cells; T7 starts at its promoter, distinct from the Kozak context; template defines sequence and endpoint.
requirements.note: Henderson abstract only.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: IVT makes RNA from a DNA template with an RNA polymerase outside living cells; T7 starts at its promoter, distinct from the Kozak context; template defines sequence and endpoint.

requirements.statement: Cap can be added during transcription or afterwards; poly(A) can be encoded or added enzymatically; alternatives, not identical ends.
requirements.note: Poly(A) encoded versus enzymatic addition: Losada review states the cap or poly(A) can be added after transcription.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Cap can be added during transcription or afterwards; poly(A) can be encoded or added enzymatically; alternatives, not identical ends.

requirements.statement: After synthesis the preparation can contain template DNA, enzymes, free building blocks, incomplete transcripts and dsRNA; each cleanup removes different things.
requirements.note: Now sourced for template DNA, enzymes, free nucleotides, abortive transcripts and dsRNA.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: After synthesis the preparation can contain template DNA, enzymes, free building blocks, incomplete transcripts and dsRNA; each cleanup removes different things.

requirements.statement: Mu demonstrates one route by which T7 generates unintended complementary RNA.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Mu demonstrates one route by which T7 generates unintended complementary RNA.

requirements.statement: The DNA is a manufacturing input, not a DNA-delivery therapy; residual DNA is a separate quality question; RNA must stay traceable to the antigen design; expression and potency assays add functional evidence.
requirements.note: Residual-DNA and impurity-control reasoning now sourced; traceability-to-antigen-design statement is not separately sourced and the patch does not assert it.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: The DNA is a manufacturing input, not a DNA-delivery therapy; residual DNA is a separate quality question; RNA must stay traceable to the antigen design; expression and potency assays add functional evidence.

requirements.statement: Measurement table: identity and modification analysis, poly(A) tail, RNA content, integrity and transcript length, dsRNA, residual DNA and expression as separate assays; the claim that free nucleotides inflate absorbance-based quantity is unsupported by any retrieved source.
requirements.note: RETAINED GAP: the absorbance-inflation sentence has no source (searched Europe PMC and read Losada, Alasmari and Nowak reviews); the patch omits it and says total mass and integrity are separate assays.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Distinguish sequence and chemistry identity, poly(A), RNA content, length and integrity, dsRNA, residual DNA and expression assays. Unincorporated nucleotides and template DNA affect UV absorbance, so purification and measurement method must be stated rather than treating an unpurified absorbance reading as transcript-specific mass.

requirements.statement: Inference from the Try it (expected total mass but many short molecules): total mass includes non-full-length material; investigate template, synthesis, handling and cleanup, and assess by the specified methods; neither mass nor one failing observation settles release.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Inference from the Try it (expected total mass but many short molecules): total mass includes non-full-length material; investigate template, synthesis, handling and cleanup, and assess by the specified methods; neither mass nor one failing observation settles release.

requirements.statement: Source scope: Henderson 2021 protocol and Mu 2018 mechanism; process reasoning, not an executable recipe or specification.
requirements.note: Identity verified. A PMID-matched DOI check was done independently (DOI title, authors, year compared).

coordinatorDisposition.kind: source-list/scope metadata; source reading retained, not additional teaching credit

requirements.statement: Takeaway restates R03, R06.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: derived takeaway; assessed but not an independent semantic requirement

requirements.statement: Modified nucleosides (pseudouridine, N1-methylpseudouridine) are alternative building blocks; the intended coding message can stay the same while chemistry changes; nucleoside versus nucleotide (figure: sequence, chemistry, byproducts).
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Modified nucleosides (pseudouridine, N1-methylpseudouridine) are alternative building blocks; the intended coding message can stay the same while chemistry changes; nucleoside versus nucleotide (figure: sequence, chemistry, byproducts).

requirements.statement: Karikó tested human TLR systems and dendritic cells: particular modifications reduced the measured activation; Andries compared m1Ψ with Ψ in cell lines and mice.
requirements.note: Andries added to the patch.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Karikó tested human TLR systems and dendritic cells: particular modifications reduced the measured activation; Andries compared m1Ψ with Ψ in cell lines and mice.

requirements.statement: Intended sequence and sensing are separate; chemistry and purity are separate; modified transcripts can still contain dsRNA; Karikó 2011 tested purification as another source of activation.
requirements.note: Karikó 2011 full text retrieved (OA).
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Intended sequence and sensing are separate; chemistry and purity are separate; modified transcripts can still contain dsRNA; Karikó 2011 tested purification as another source of activation.

requirements.statement: Mulroney: sequence-dependent +1 frameshifts with m1Ψ RNA in experimental systems, reduced by synonymous changes; not every modified construct mistranslates and no adverse clinical outcomes were established.
requirements.note: Abstract also reports cellular immunity in mice and humans to +1 products after BNT162b2 vaccination, which the Guide page omits; the patch includes it. Full text retrieved (OA).
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Mulroney: sequence-dependent +1 frameshifts with m1Ψ RNA in experimental systems, reduced by synonymous changes; not every modified construct mistranslates and no adverse clinical outcomes were established.

requirements.statement: RNA sensing can influence antigen production and immune activation; lower innate activation in one assay is not lower antigen-specific immunity; more protein is not a stronger T-cell response; chemistry does not choose the target.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: RNA sensing can influence antigen production and immune activation; lower innate activation in one assay is not lower antigen-specific immunity; more protein is not a stronger T-cell response; chemistry does not choose the target.

requirements.statement: Measurement table: chemistry and identity analysis, impurity testing, protein identity and quantity, innate-sensing readouts; matched sequence, amount, cap, UTRs, purity, formulation; single translation or cytokine readout cannot establish display, recognition, safety or efficacy.
requirements.note: Measurement points mapped to the studies' own readouts: reporter output, cytokines, viability, translation in primary cells.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Measurement table: chemistry and identity analysis, impurity testing, protein identity and quantity, innate-sensing readouts; matched sequence, amount, cap, UTRs, purity, formulation; single translation or cytokine readout cannot establish display, recognition, safety or efficacy.

requirements.statement: Inference from the Try it (more reporter, less cytokine): one matched cell-line comparison does not show a stronger antigen-specific T-cell response; check protein identity and comparable impurity/delivery conditions, then test downstream biology.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Inference from the Try it (more reporter, less cytokine): one matched cell-line comparison does not show a stronger antigen-specific T-cell response; check protein identity and comparable impurity/delivery conditions, then test downstream biology.

requirements.statement: Source scope: Karikó 2005 and 2011, Andries 2015, Mulroney 2024 bounded to experimental systems.
requirements.note: Mulroney title contains markup in Europe PMC (sup tags); Crossref title verified; all four identities match.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: source-list/scope metadata; source reading retained, not additional teaching credit

requirements.statement: Takeaway restates R03, R05, R07.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: derived takeaway; assessed but not an independent semantic requirement

requirements.statement: dsRNA has paired complementary regions; T7 can make an antisense strand that pairs with the intended strand; Mu showed promoter-independent initiation at a DNA end and activation of a long-dsRNA sensor; one documented origin, not the only one.
requirements.note: Mu is not linked in the draft; patch adds it.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: dsRNA has paired complementary regions; T7 can make an antisense strand that pairs with the intended strand; Mu showed promoter-independent initiation at a DNA end and activation of a long-dsRNA sensor; one documented origin, not the only one.

requirements.statement: A truncated transcript is not dsRNA; folding within a message is not an unwanted duplex (figure: paired byproduct, truncated strand, fold).
requirements.note: Upgraded from existing-draft-text: a truncated or folded RNA is not a long duplex is supported by the study's length-dependent removal and the long-dsRNA definition of the sensor activation; definitional element remains the Guide's.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: A truncated transcript is not dsRNA; folding within a message is not an unwanted duplex (figure: paired byproduct, truncated strand, fold).

requirements.statement: Innate sensing depends on length, structure, chemistry, delivery and cell context; modified nucleosides do not establish absence of dsRNA; Karikó tested purification as an additional determinant.
requirements.note: Already largely in the draft.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Innate sensing depends on length, structure, chemistry, delivery and cell context; modified nucleosides do not establish absence of dsRNA; Karikó tested purification as an additional determinant.

requirements.statement: Baiersdörfer tested cellulose binding with measurements of recovery, integrity and cellular effects; the method did not remove every tested short duplex equally; method performance is not a clinical impurity limit.
requirements.note: Baiersdörfer full text retrieved (OA); the 21 base-pair result is from the full text, not the abstract.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Baiersdörfer tested cellulose binding with measurements of recovery, integrity and cellular effects; the method did not remove every tested short duplex equally; method performance is not a clinical impurity limit.

requirements.statement: A vaccine may seek immune activation but an uncontrolled byproduct is not antigen-specific immunity; cleaner RNA improving a measurement in one system does not prove tumour recognition.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: A vaccine may seek immune activation but an uncontrolled byproduct is not antigen-specific immunity; cleaner RNA improving a measurement in one system does not prove tumour recognition.

requirements.statement: Measurement table: dsRNA-binding antibody assay plus size and integrity and expression assays; units and recovery; detection and quantitation limits; calibrator, structure-recognition and matrix failure modes; antibody recognition depends on length and chemistry.
requirements.note: Detection length floor and assay types sourced. Calibrator and matrix failure modes are general analytical reasoning, not claimed beyond the length floor.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Measurement table: dsRNA-binding antibody assay plus size and integrity and expression assays; units and recovery; detection and quantitation limits; calibrator, structure-recognition and matrix failure modes; antibody recognition depends on length and chemistry.

requirements.statement: Inference from the Try it (lower dsRNA signal but substantial fragmentation): the dsRNA readout improved but integrity worsened; reassess recovery, degradation and other specifications; neither result answers every quality question.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Inference from the Try it (lower dsRNA signal but substantial fragmentation): the dsRNA readout improved but integrity worsened; reassess recovery, degradation and other specifications; neither result answers every quality question.

requirements.statement: Source scope: Mu 2018, Karikó 2011, Baiersdörfer 2019; no acceptable clinical impurity limit defined.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: source-list/scope metadata; source reading retained, not additional teaching credit

requirements.statement: Takeaway restates R04, R06, R07.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: derived takeaway; assessed but not an independent semantic requirement

requirements.statement: An mRNA construct combines a coding message with features influencing translation, stability and processing; 5′ and 3′ ends; cap, 5′ UTR, Kozak context, ORF, 3′ UTR, poly(A) tail (table; figure).
requirements.note: Source-blocked Cooper chapter replaced by OpenStax Biology 2e (accessible textbook) for cap, UTR, poly-A and scanning-to-AUG definitions; cap chemistry detail (modified guanosine) is not stated in the retrieved page and is not asserted.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: An mRNA construct combines a coding message with features influencing translation, stability and processing; 5′ and 3′ ends; cap, 5′ UTR, Kozak context, ORF, 3′ UTR, poly(A) tail (table; figure).

requirements.statement: Kozak's start-context experiments and Gallie's cap/tail experiments tested particular constructs and cell systems; Holtkamp altered 3′ features in antigen RNA delivered to dendritic cells.
requirements.note: Kozak and Gallie are not linked in the draft; Holtkamp is.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Kozak's start-context experiments and Gallie's cap/tail experiments tested particular constructs and cell systems; Holtkamp altered 3′ features in antigen RNA delivered to dendritic cells.

requirements.statement: A target list is not the finished construct; multi-epitope designs add windows, spacers and trafficking features; UTR change alters expression, spacer change alters the combined protein; chemistry and formulation are additional specifications.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: A target list is not the finished construct; multi-epitope designs add windows, spacers and trafficking features; UTR change alters expression, spacer change alters the combined protein; chemistry and formulation are additional specifications.

requirements.statement: Measurement table: sequence identity, size and integrity, cap/tail characterisation, expression comparison; no universal good-construct score; reporter comparison supports that model.
requirements.note: Measurement separation (RT-PCR transcript, eGFP protein, peptide-MHC, T-cell stimulation) sourced.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Measurement table: sequence identity, size and integrity, cap/tail characterisation, expression comparison; no universal good-construct score; reporter comparison supports that model.

requirements.statement: Inference from the Try it (3' UTR change doubling reporter signal): the antigen sequence is unchanged and the result supports greater reporter output only; it is not a different antigen, processing, recognition or clinical benefit; confirm identity and integrity first.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Inference from the Try it (3' UTR change doubling reporter signal): the antigen sequence is unchanged and the result supports greater reporter output only; it is not a different antigen, processing, recognition or clinical benefit; confirm identity and integrity first.

requirements.statement: Source scope: Cooper chapter (NBK9849) access-failed; Kozak 1986, Gallie 1991, Holtkamp 2006 verified; OpenStax used as the accessible textbook alternative.
requirements.note: Retained access limit: Cooper (reCAPTCHA; Europe PMC 500). The requirement is covered by the alternative; the Cooper citation itself stays unread.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: source-list/scope metadata; source reading retained, not additional teaching credit

requirements.statement: Takeaway restates R01, R03, R05.

coordinatorDisposition.kind: derived takeaway; assessed but not an independent semantic requirement

requirements.statement: An epitope is a feature recognised by an immune receptor; encoded windows are not necessarily the displayed peptide; string-of-beads designs concatenate windows with spacers; junction peptides can span neighbours (figure).
requirements.note: Epitope/peptide definition sourced by Caron review (OA); HLA nomenclature itself is background.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: An epitope is a feature recognised by an immune receptor; encoded windows are not necessarily the displayed peptide; string-of-beads designs concatenate windows with spacers; junction peptides can span neighbours (figure).

requirements.statement: Schubert and Kohlbacher modelled class-I cleavage and binding to optimise spacers; gains are predicted, not measured human protection.
requirements.note: Schubert full text available (OA) but only the abstract was read for these numbers.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Schubert and Kohlbacher modelled class-I cleavage and binding to optimise spacers; gains are predicted, not measured human protection.

requirements.statement: Signal peptide routes the protein, not the carrier; Kreiter combined an N-terminal leader with a C-terminal trafficking signal in human and mouse dendritic cells.
requirements.note: Abstract only.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Signal peptide routes the protein, not the carrier; Kreiter combined an N-terminal leader with a C-terminal trafficking signal in human and mouse dendritic cells.

requirements.statement: Helper segments aim to engage CD4 T cells through HLA class II but are not universally necessary; multi-target vaccines can distribute targets across strands.
requirements.note: Helper-segment-through-class-II aim is supported by Kreiter's class II presentation and CD4 expansion; 'not universally necessary or sufficient' is asserted by the Guide, and the patch states only the sourced design facts.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Helper segments aim to engage CD4 T cells through HLA class II but are not universally necessary; multi-target vaccines can distribute targets across strands.

requirements.statement: Multiple targets broaden opportunities but target count is not response breadth; tumour expression, processing, HLA match and recognition remain gates; spacer change is not synonymous codon redesign.
requirements.note: Sahin is abstract-only and a small first-in-human uncontrolled study.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Multiple targets broaden opportunities but target count is not response breadth; tumour expression, processing, HLA match and recognition remain gates; spacer change is not synonymous codon redesign.

requirements.statement: Measurement table: sequence verification, expression assays, immunopeptidomics for recovered HLA peptides, functional assays; prediction scores are not presentation thresholds; non-detection does not prove absence.
requirements.note: Resolved: recovered HLA peptides by mass spectrometry, prediction versus presentation, non-detection does not prove absence.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Measurement table: sequence verification, expression assays, immunopeptidomics for recovered HLA peptides, functional assays; prediction scores are not presentation thresholds; non-detection does not prove absence.

requirements.statement: Inference from the Try it (spacer replaced, A and B unchanged): the combined protein and boundaries changed; retain old evidence but renew expression, processing and display testing for the new revision; the old result did not establish B's display or tumour recognition.
requirements.coordinatorRequirement: Inference from the Try it (spacer replaced, A and B unchanged): the combined protein and boundaries changed; retain old evidence but renew expression, processing and display testing for the new revision; the old result did not establish B's display or tumour recognition.

requirements.statement: Source scope: Schubert 2016, Kreiter 2008, Sahin 2017, Rojas 2023.
requirements.note: All four identities verified.
